_about: The legal team's clause-by-clause risk classification for MSAs, transcribed from the workbook 'MSA Clause Risk Classification - Standard Instructions clause by clause'. One entry per clause type, named as the taxonomy names it. risk_allocation is the risk level the legal team assigns to the clause; fallback_guidelines is the compromise position to propose when the clause misses the standard. scripts/build_policies_from_taxonomy.py reads this file: a clause type listed here takes its risk tier and fallback position from here.

Definitions & Interpretation.acceptable_standard: Clear, precise, consistently used defined terms; neutral interpretation rules; definitions do not silently expand obligations or narrow protections
Definitions & Interpretation.unacceptable_triggers: Overbroad definitions that expand liability or scope (e.g., Confidential Information, Losses, Deliverables); undefined capitalised terms; circular definitions; interpretation rules favouring one party
Definitions & Interpretation.fallback_guidelines: Tighten definitions with qualifiers; add missing definitions; align to operative clauses; make interpretation rules mutual

Purpose.acceptable_standard: Short statement of commercial intent and the framework nature of the MSA; non-operative
Purpose.unacceptable_triggers: Recitals that create binding obligations, warranties or exclusivity; purpose inconsistent with scope
Purpose.fallback_guidelines: State that recitals are non-operative; delete or conform to Scope of Services

Scope of Services.acceptable_standard: Services specifically described; assumptions and exclusions stated; additions handled through Change Control
Scope of Services.unacceptable_triggers: Open-ended scope ("all related services"); unlimited scope creep without fee adjustment; no exclusions; conflict with SOW
Scope of Services.fallback_guidelines: Add defined service descriptions, assumptions and exclusions; route additions through Change Control

Statements of Work & Work Orders.acceptable_standard: SOWs signed by both parties, stating scope, deliverables, timeline, fees, acceptance criteria and personnel; MSA terms apply; no work or fees before a signed SOW
Statements of Work & Work Orders.unacceptable_triggers: SOW overrides MSA without express reference; unilateral issuance of work orders; fees due without signed SOW; missing fees or acceptance criteria; SOW continues after MSA ends with no governing terms
Statements of Work & Work Orders.fallback_guidelines: Require signed SOW with minimum content; SOW overrides MSA only by express named clause; add pre-authorisation requirement for work orders

Customer Obligations.acceptable_standard: Limited to reasonable, specified cooperation (access, information, timely decisions); provider relief only if it gives prompt notice and is actually prevented
Customer Obligations.unacceptable_triggers: Open-ended dependencies; deemed breach or automatic fee, SLA or deadline relief for any customer delay; unspecified resource commitments; customer responsible for provider's failures
Customer Obligations.fallback_guidelines: List obligations specifically; require written notice and a cure period; limit relief to delay actually caused

Service Provider Obligations.acceptable_standard: Services performed with professional skill and care, to industry standards, per SOW and applicable law, by qualified personnel; defects re-performed
Service Provider Obligations.unacceptable_triggers: No performance standard or "best efforts" only; services "as is"; no obligation to meet timelines; unilateral right to change services or key personnel; no re-performance
Service Provider Obligations.fallback_guidelines: Add professional-standard and re-performance obligations; key personnel replacement with consent; timelines binding unless customer-caused

Term & Termination.acceptable_standard: Defined initial term and renewal mechanism; customer termination for convenience on reasonable notice; mutual termination for cause with cure period (typically 30 days); transition assistance; pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
Term & Termination.unacceptable_triggers: Auto-renewal with long notice window or price uplift; provider-only convenience termination; no cure period; excessive termination fees; no transition assistance; no return of data
Term & Termination.fallback_guidelines: Opt-in renewal or 60-day notice window; mutual convenience termination on 60-90 days; 30-day cure; limit termination fees to unrecovered committed costs

Deliverables & Acceptance.acceptable_standard: Objective acceptance criteria; reasonable review period (typically 10-30 days); written rejection with reasons; rework at provider cost; payment tied to acceptance
Deliverables & Acceptance.unacceptable_triggers: Deemed acceptance on short silence; no right to reject; acceptance by use; subjective criteria controlled by provider; acceptance waives warranty claims
Deliverables & Acceptance.fallback_guidelines: Extend review period; deemed acceptance only after reminder notice; objective criteria in SOW; acceptance does not waive warranty

Service Levels.acceptable_standard: Measurable SLAs with defined measurement and reporting; service credits; right to terminate for chronic failure
Service Levels.unacceptable_triggers: Aspirational targets only; credits as sole and exclusive remedy with no termination right; broad exclusions; short claim windows; no reporting
Service Levels.fallback_guidelines: Add reporting, credit schedule and chronic-failure termination right; extend claim window; narrow exclusions

Support & Maintenance.acceptable_standard: Defined support hours, response and resolution times by severity; escalation path; updates and patches included
Support & Maintenance.unacceptable_triggers: No support commitment; support at provider's discretion; right to discontinue without notice; extra charges for defect fixes
Support & Maintenance.fallback_guidelines: Add severity-based response times; 12 months' notice before end-of-support; defect fixes at no charge

Change Control.acceptable_standard: Written change request process; approval by both parties; documented impact on scope, fees and timeline
Change Control.unacceptable_triggers: Unilateral changes to scope, fees or terms; changes effective by email or conduct; no pricing transparency; refusing a change is a breach
Change Control.fallback_guidelines: Require signed change order; provider must supply impact assessment; no work or charges before approval

Fees & Payment.acceptable_standard: Fees clearly stated (fixed or rate card); invoicing in arrears or on milestones; payment net 30-45 days; good-faith dispute right; expenses pre-approved; price increases capped and notified in advance
Fees & Payment.unacceptable_triggers: Unilateral price increases; payment terms under 15 days; late fees above 1.5% per month; no dispute right; suspension for disputed amounts; non-refundable prepayments; uncapped expenses; non-cancellable commitments
Fees & Payment.fallback_guidelines: Cap increases (e.g., CPI or fixed %) with 90 days' notice; net 30; withhold disputed amounts without penalty; expense pre-approval and caps

Confidentiality.acceptable_standard: Mutual; defined scope with standard exclusions; reasonable care; use only for the agreement; compelled-disclosure notice; return or destruction; term of 3-5 years after termination (trade secrets for as long as they remain secret)
Confidentiality.unacceptable_triggers: One-way obligations; no exclusions; perpetual term for all information; residuals clause; no return or destruction; broad permitted disclosures; no remedies
Confidentiality.fallback_guidelines: Make mutual; add standard exclusions; need-to-know and flow-down to recipients; time-limit non-trade-secret information

Data Protection & Privacy.acceptable_standard: Compliance with applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, India DPDP Act, as relevant); Data Processing Agreement with documented instructions; security measures; breach notice (typically within 72 hours); sub-processor controls; lawful transfer mechanisms; deletion or return at exit
Data Protection & Privacy.unacceptable_triggers: No DPA where personal data is processed; provider may use customer data for its own purposes or model training without consent; no breach notification; unrestricted cross-border transfer; no security standards; no deletion on exit
Data Protection & Privacy.fallback_guidelines: Attach DPA and security schedule; restrict use to service delivery; 72-hour breach notice (up to 5 days as a fallback); approved sub-processor list with objection right

Intellectual Property.acceptable_standard: Customer owns its data and bespoke deliverables (on payment); provider retains pre-existing IP and tools and licenses embedded IP to customer; clear licence scope; no implied licences; limited feedback licence
Intellectual Property.unacceptable_triggers: Provider owns all deliverables with no licence back; assignment of customer's pre-existing IP; broad licence to customer data; no licence to embedded provider IP; ownership of derivatives of customer data
Intellectual Property.fallback_guidelines: Customer owns deliverables, or receives perpetual royalty-free licence to use them; carve out pre-existing IP; limit licence to customer data to service delivery

Representations & Warranties.acceptable_standard: Mutual authority and capacity; provider warrants conformity to specification, professional performance, non-infringement, legal compliance and freedom from malware; remedy is re-performance or refund
Representations & Warranties.unacceptable_triggers: Blanket "as is" disclaimer; warranty period under 30 days; no non-infringement warranty; knowledge-qualified warranties only; exclusive remedy that is illusory
Representations & Warranties.fallback_guidelines: Extend warranty period (60-90 days minimum); add non-infringement and compliance warranties; re-performance plus refund fallback

Indemnification.acceptable_standard: Provider indemnifies for third-party IP infringement, data breach and legal violations, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, bodily injury and property damage; customer indemnifies for customer data and misuse; defined notice, control and cooperation process; broadly mutual
Indemnification.unacceptable_triggers: One-way indemnity against customer; unlimited customer indemnity; indemnity for provider's own negligence; no IP indemnity; no duty to defend; settlement without consent; first-party losses indemnified in provider's favour
Indemnification.fallback_guidelines: Make mutual and proportionate; limit customer indemnity to customer data and misuse; add procedure and settlement consent; keep IP indemnity in all cases

Limitation of Liability.acceptable_standard: Mutual cap at fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months (higher multiple for high-risk services); mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential loss; carve-outs from caps for confidentiality, data breach (super-cap acceptable), indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and death or personal injury
Limitation of Liability.unacceptable_triggers: One-sided cap; cap below 12 months' fees or a low fixed amount; no carve-outs; customer's payment obligations not excluded from its cap; exclusion of direct losses such as data restoration; uncapped liability for customer only
Limitation of Liability.fallback_guidelines: Super-cap for data breach and confidentiality (e.g., 2-3x fees); mutual cap; minimum 12 months' fees; clearly define recoverable direct losses

Insurance.acceptable_standard: Provider maintains commercially reasonable cover (general liability, professional or E&O, cyber, workers' compensation) at stated minimums; certificates on request; notice of cancellation
Insurance.unacceptable_triggers: No insurance requirement; limits well below deal exposure; insurance limits used as liability cap; claims-made cover with no tail
Insurance.fallback_guidelines: Specify minimum limits per cover type; certificate on request; 30 days' notice of cancellation; 2-year tail for claims-made

Compliance.acceptable_standard: Each party complies with applicable laws (anti-bribery, labour, environmental, tax); code of conduct; notification of violations
Compliance.unacceptable_triggers: Compliance obligations only on customer; compliance with provider policies that can change unilaterally; no anti-corruption commitments
Compliance.fallback_guidelines: Make mutual; attach policies by version; add anti-bribery and violation-notice clauses

Audit & Records.acceptable_standard: Provider keeps records for 3-7 years; customer may audit on reasonable notice (at least 10 business days), annually, in business hours, subject to confidentiality; regulator access; costs allocated fairly
Audit & Records.unacceptable_triggers: No audit rights where regulated or personal data is involved; unlimited provider audit of customer; audit costs always on customer; no regulator access
Audit & Records.fallback_guidelines: Third-party or remote audit alternatives; annual limit with exceptions for incidents and regulators; provider bears cost if material non-compliance is found

Subcontractors.acceptable_standard: Subcontracting only with prior written consent or notice with objection right; provider remains fully liable; confidentiality and data protection terms flow down
Subcontractors.unacceptable_triggers: Free subcontracting without notice; provider disclaims liability for subcontractors; no flow-down; offshoring without notice
Subcontractors.fallback_guidelines: Approved-subcontractor list; notice of changes; flow-down of key obligations; provider fully responsible for subcontractors

Assignment.acceptable_standard: No assignment without consent (not unreasonably withheld); permitted assignment to affiliates or successors with notice; termination right if assigned to a competitor
Assignment.unacceptable_triggers: One-sided right for provider to assign; change of control without notice; assignment to a competitor
Assignment.fallback_guidelines: Mutual consent requirement; allow affiliate and merger assignment with notice; termination right on competitor assignment

Force Majeure.acceptable_standard: Defined events beyond reasonable control; prompt notice and mitigation; relief from performance only; right to terminate after prolonged event (30-60 days); excludes subcontractor failure and foreseeable or preventable events
Force Majeure.unacceptable_triggers: Overbroad events (own labour disputes, supplier failure, cyberattacks that a BCP should prevent); no notice or mitigation; no termination right; customer must still pay for undelivered services
Force Majeure.fallback_guidelines: Narrow event list; require notice and mitigation; termination after 30-60 days; fee abatement during the event

Governing Law & Dispute Resolution.acceptable_standard: Neutral or customer-favourable governing law; escalation, then mediation, then courts or arbitration; defined seat, language and rules; reasonable venue
Governing Law & Dispute Resolution.unacceptable_triggers: Unfavourable foreign law or venue; unilateral right to choose forum; mandatory arbitration with unfair cost allocation; no carve-out for injunctive relief; one-way fee shifting
Governing Law & Dispute Resolution.fallback_guidelines: Neutral law and venue; defendant's home forum; institutional arbitration with agreed seat; mutual costs

Notices.acceptable_standard: Written notice to named addresses or emails; clear deemed-receipt rules; address updates by notice
Notices.unacceptable_triggers: Notice by website posting; notice effective without receipt; unrealistic delivery rules
Notices.fallback_guidelines: Specify email and courier addresses; use standard deemed-receipt rules

Independent Contractor.acceptable_standard: Parties are independent contractors; provider responsible for its personnel's wages, taxes and benefits
Independent Contractor.unacceptable_triggers: Wording that creates employment or joint-employer risk (customer directs provider personnel); personnel claim customer benefits
Independent Contractor.fallback_guidelines: Add independent contractor wording and provider responsibility for personnel

Entire Agreement.acceptable_standard: MSA, SOWs and attachments supersede prior agreements on the subject; fraud is not excluded; documents listed
Entire Agreement.unacceptable_triggers: Excludes reliance on fraudulent statements; incorporates changeable online terms or policies; unintentionally supersedes an existing NDA
Entire Agreement.fallback_guidelines: Add fraud carve-out; limit to attached documents; preserve existing NDA

Order of Precedence.acceptable_standard: Clear hierarchy (e.g., MSA body, then DPA or security schedule, then SOW, then other attachments); SOW overrides MSA only by express statement; customer PO and provider online terms excluded
Order of Precedence.unacceptable_triggers: Provider quotes, click-through or online terms override the MSA; no hierarchy; conflicting terms with no resolution rule
Order of Precedence.fallback_guidelines: Insert a hierarchy clause; exclude PO and online terms; require express override language in SOW

Amendments and Modifications.acceptable_standard: In writing and signed by both authorised signatories; no amendment by email, conduct or website update
Amendments and Modifications.unacceptable_triggers: Unilateral right to amend by posting; amendment by conduct; click acceptance
Amendments and Modifications.fallback_guidelines: Require signed written amendments; policy changes need 60 days' notice and a termination right

Waiver.acceptable_standard: Waiver must be in writing; failure to enforce is not a waiver; mutual
Waiver.unacceptable_triggers: Deemed waiver after a time period; claims waived by acceptance or payment; one-sided waiver
Waiver.fallback_guidelines: Written-waiver requirement; no waiver by payment or acceptance

Severability.acceptable_standard: Invalid provisions severed; remainder continues; parties reform to closest lawful intent
Severability.unacceptable_triggers: Severance that removes core risk allocation (e.g., liability cap) without renegotiation; one-sided operation
Severability.fallback_guidelines: Add renegotiation obligation where severance affects a core term

No Agency or Authority.acceptable_standard: Neither party may bind the other; no partnership or joint venture
No Agency or Authority.unacceptable_triggers: Provider authority to bind customer; implied agency; customer liable for provider's statements

Non-Exclusivity.acceptable_standard: Neither party is exclusive; customer may use other providers; provider may serve others subject to confidentiality
Non-Exclusivity.unacceptable_triggers: Customer exclusivity or minimum purchase commitments; non-compete on customer; provider exclusivity without consideration
Non-Exclusivity.fallback_guidelines: Delete exclusivity or minimum-spend terms; if required, tie to pricing benefits

Export Controls and Sanctions.acceptable_standard: Each party complies with applicable export control and sanctions laws (e.g., US, EU, UN and local); no dealings with restricted parties; prompt notice; right to suspend or terminate for violation
Export Controls and Sanctions.unacceptable_triggers: Obligations on customer only; customer warrants all affiliates are unrestricted; clause missing in a cross-border deal; strict liability for violations; provider excludes its own supply chain
Export Controls and Sanctions.fallback_guidelines: Make mutual; add screening and notice duties; limit warranties to knowledge; add suspension and termination right

Publicity and Use of Names.acceptable_standard: No use of name, logo or announcements without prior written consent; consent revocable
Publicity and Use of Names.unacceptable_triggers: Provider may use customer name or logo as a reference without consent; unilateral press release; no revocation
Publicity and Use of Names.fallback_guidelines: Require prior written approval of each use; allow revocation

Equitable Relief.acceptable_standard: Either party may seek injunctive relief for confidentiality or IP breach without proving damages (as permitted by law); non-exclusive
Equitable Relief.unacceptable_triggers: One-sided right; waiver of customer's right to injunction; provider may suspend or restrain services during a dispute
Equitable Relief.fallback_guidelines: Make mutual; limit to confidentiality and IP; no suspension of services during a good-faith dispute

Conflict of Interest.acceptable_standard: Provider discloses actual or potential conflicts; no engagements that impair performance; gifts and hospitality rules
Conflict of Interest.unacceptable_triggers: No disclosure obligation; provider may serve direct competitors using customer information; no gifts rules
Conflict of Interest.fallback_guidelines: Add disclosure duty, information barriers and gifts policy

Survival.acceptable_standard: Express list of surviving clauses (confidentiality, IP, indemnity, liability, accrued payments, data return, governing law)
Survival.unacceptable_triggers: No survival clause; critical clauses omitted; only provider-favourable terms survive; customer obligations survive indefinitely
Survival.fallback_guidelines: Add a survival list; time-limit survival where appropriate

Counterparts.acceptable_standard: Execution in counterparts; electronic signatures valid
Counterparts.unacceptable_triggers: Electronic signatures excluded where law allows them; unclear signing authority
Counterparts.fallback_guidelines: Add counterparts and e-signature wording; confirm signatory authority

Time of the Essence.acceptable_standard: Applies only to specifically identified milestones or payment dates, and mutually
Time of the Essence.unacceptable_triggers: General time-of-the-essence applied to customer only or to all obligations; provider deadlines exempt
Time of the Essence.fallback_guidelines: Limit to named milestones; make mutual; add grace period

Taxes.acceptable_standard: Fees exclusive of indirect taxes (VAT or GST) shown separately; each party bears its own income taxes; cooperation on treaty relief; withholding gross-up not required or limited; compliant tax invoices
Taxes.unacceptable_triggers: Customer bears all taxes including provider's income taxes; mandatory gross-up of withholding tax; undisclosed taxes added later; non-compliant invoices; no cooperation on tax forms
Taxes.fallback_guidelines: Allocate each tax type explicitly; no gross-up (or capped); require compliant invoices and tax certificates

Miscellaneous / Other Provisions.acceptable_standard: Standard boilerplate (further assurances, costs, language, interpretation) that does not alter risk allocation
Miscellaneous / Other Provisions.unacceptable_triggers: Hidden substantive terms (non-solicit, exclusivity, IP assignment, liability shifts, auto-renewal) in boilerplate; one-sided terms
Miscellaneous / Other Provisions.fallback_guidelines: Move substantive terms to the correct clause for review; delete or make mutual
